enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (name, school, parents, family background etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **f)** Write about an important event which has taken place in your country, town or village within the past decade, pointing out the significance of the event to you and your country, town or village.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: the event (the opening of the new bridge in our town) and when it happened.
2. Background: the problem before the event.
3. How the event took place.
4. Significance for the town, the country and for me.
5. Conclusion.

**Model composition (479 words)**

Within the past decade, many things have happened in our town, but nothing has been as important to us as the opening of the new bridge over the River Mungo in March 2019. It was a day I will always remember because it changed the life of my community.

Before the bridge was built, we crossed the river on a rotten wooden bridge that the heavy rains of every year damaged. Each time the water rose, the bridge was closed, and our town was cut off from the main road. Farmers could not take their foodstuffs to the market, the sick could not reach the hospital, and pupils who lived on the other side missed school for days. I still remember the sad day when a truck fell into the river and two people lost their lives. After that accident, the whole town cried for a new bridge.

Our appeals were finally heard when the government and a foreign partner agreed to finance a modern concrete bridge. The work lasted two years. Engineers and workers came from different places, and many young men from our town were employed, which brought money into many homes.

The inauguration took place on a sunny Saturday morning. The road was decorated with flags and palm leaves, and thousands of people gathered at the entrance of the bridge. The school band played the national anthem, the traditional dancers entertained the crowd, and the Divisional Officer cut the ribbon amid cheers. Then the first vehicles crossed the bridge, followed by children singing and waving. The chief thanked the government in his speech and asked the people to protect the structure. In the evening, there was a big feast in the town hall.

The significance of the bridge to my town cannot be overstated. It has made transport safe and fast, so that farmers now sell their produce at better prices, and traders and travellers visit us more often. New shops, restaurants and a petrol station have opened near the bridge, giving jobs to many young people. Our hospital is now accessible at any time, and no pupil misses school because of floods. For the country, the bridge is part of the road which links the region to the economic capital and strengthens national trade.

For me personally, the bridge is a symbol of hope. It taught me that determination and patience can solve even the biggest problems, and it made me want to become an engineer so that I may also build for my people.

In conclusion, the opening of the bridge was a historic event which brought development and joy to my town, and I will always be proud to have been there. Whenever I cross the bridge today, I remember the faces of the people who danced that day, and I thank all those who worked hard to make our dream come true.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | A real important event of the past decade, clearly narrated, with its significance to the writer AND to the country, town or village, in clear paragraphs |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Choosing an event that is too old (outside the past decade) or telling the event without showing its significance.
2. Giving the significance for the town only and forgetting 'to you' (the writer).
